title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck has a pair of tori T_ρ, T_σ, apparently commutative algebraic subgroups of a group like GL_2, each with a 'determinant' character to G_m; N'_σ is a variant of T_σ, probably a normaliser-type group. From them he builds:
- the fibre product 𝒯°_{ρ,σ} = T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ, with determinant map y: 𝒯° → G_m;
- the larger groups 𝒯_{ρ,σ} ⊃ 𝒯°_{ρ,σ};
- the 'radical' groups R°_{ρ,σ} ⊂ R_{ρ,σ}.
On (105) and the paraphrase on the previous page, R° is the fibre product of 𝒯° with the squaring map:
  R° = 𝒯° ×_{y, G_m, λ↦λ²} G_m.
Thus R° is a μ_2-extension of 𝒯° obtained by adjoining a square root of the determinant.

The homomorphism i_R (118)–(120). The scalar embedding i_τ: λ ↦ (λ,λ) satisfies y∘i_τ = λ². By the universal property of the fibre product there is a unique i_R: G_m → R° with can∘i_R = i_τ. Concretely i_R(λ) = (i_τ(λ), λ). Equivalently (121) is a morphism of short exact sequences:
  1→μ_2→G_m→G_m→1 (squaring) mapping into 1→μ_2→R°→𝒯°→1.
The page draws only the bottom row and a vertical stroke; the top row is implicit.

The retraction (122). The second projection ★: R° → G_m (the chosen square root of the determinant) satisfies ★∘i_R = id. So i_R is a split monomorphism. Since everything is commutative, this gives the direct-product decomposition (123):
  R° ≃ SR° × G_m, where SR° = ker ★.
The kernel ker ★ = {(t,1): y(t)=1} = ST_ρ × ST_σ, the determinant-one parts. Likewise R ≃ SR × G_m ≃ S'T_ρ × SN'_σ × G_m, where:
- S'T_ρ = {a : (det a)² = 1};
- SN'_σ = {b : det b = 1}.
Grothendieck remarks that this sharpens his earlier (96).

The μ_2 inside R. He then begins to make explicit, in these coordinates, the inclusion μ_2 ↪ R° ⊂ R, which is R ∩ SG (written SG_1 on the next page), together with the maps R → 𝒯, R° → 𝒯°. A first attempt is crossed out. The next page finishes the computation:
- the map (a,b,λ) ↦ (λa, λb) has kernel μ_2 embedded diagonally, λ ↦ (λ,λ,λ);
- hence 𝒯_{ρ,σ} ≃ (S'T_ρ × SN'_σ × G_m)/μ_2.
This is the familiar pattern GL_2 ≅ (SL_2 × G_m)/μ_2, transported to these tori and normaliser-type groups.

Purpose. The 'gammes sur les radicaux' are exercises describing explicitly the algebraic groups (over Q or Z) attached to the elliptic elements ρ, σ, presumably the order-3 and order-2 generators of PSL_2(Z) or GL_2(Z). This feeds into the 'loop equation' study in the Longue Marche / Teichmüller-tower circle of ideas.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim SR° ≃ ST_ρ × ST_σ requires that the kernel of det on T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ is ST_ρ × ST_σ, which is immediate.
Diagram (121) is incomplete on the page: only the bottom exact row and a vertical arrow are drawn. The top row 1→μ_2→R°→𝒯°→1 must be supplied.
The crossed-out final lines show an abandoned first attempt at describing μ_2 in the product coordinates. It is completed correctly on the next page.

ideas.what: Adjoining a square root of a character by fibre product with the squaring map: R° = 𝒯° ×_{G_m} G_m, a μ_2-extension.
ideas.modern_name: Pullback along the Kummer sequence; double cover attached to a character (e.g. metaplectic/spin-type extension of a torus)
ideas.where_published: Similar constructions appear generally in SGA 3, but not specifically

ideas.what: Splitting R° ≃ SR° × G_m via the section i_R and retraction ★, and R ≃ S'T_ρ × SN'_σ × G_m.
ideas.modern_name: Direct-product decomposition of a commutative group scheme given a split epimorphism onto G_m

ideas.what: 𝒯_{ρ,σ} ≃ (S'T_ρ × SN'_σ × G_m)/μ_2 with diagonal μ_2 (completed on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Isogeny decomposition (derived/determinant-one part × centre)/finite central subgroup, as in GL_2 = (SL_2 × G_m)/μ_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard structure theory of reductive groups

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine explicit computations with tori and their μ_2-extensions, a 'gammes' exercise in Grothendieck's own words. They are correct and clean but contain nothing absent from standard algebraic-group theory. Their only interest is as internal detail of the loop-equation manuscript.
transcription_corrections: (121) should be read as a morphism of exact sequences. The drawn row 1→μ_2→G_m→G_m→1 (squaring) sits above an implied row 1→μ_2→R°_{ρ,σ}→𝒯°_{ρ,σ}→1, joined by a vertical arrow.
'SG' in 'μ_2 = R_{ρ,σ} ∩ SG' is written SG_1 on the next page.
In (120) the vertical arrow 'can' goes from R°_{ρ,σ} up to 𝒯°_{ρ,σ}, and i_R is the diagonal arrow G_m → R°_{ρ,σ}.
The crossed-out last lines are roughly: 'et trouve dans l'explicitation (104), que μ_2 correspond au … x … μ_2, qui …'. They are deleted text.
